title: Canary flipbook: coordinated escalation, hotpatch lifecycle, and customer-facing communications
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: Over the last 3 months we've seen intermittent canary-quality regressions that impact response fidelity for a small subset of tenants across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private planes. This ticket creates a single operational "flipbook" (playbook + choreography) that teams use when a canary or pilot rollout shows a regression and a customer escalation is opened. The flipbook focuses on 1) rapid containment, 2) coordinated hotpatch or rollback, 3) customer communication templates, and 4) post-incident reconciliation (KV-cache, inference config, and rollout gating).

Scope: This ticket covers procedural artifacts and automation needed to:
- Standardize triage sequence for canary anomalies (metrics to inspect, logs to gather, tenant slice extraction).
- Define decision matrix for roll-forward vs roll-back vs surgical hotpatch (criteria, SLO thresholds, and owner handoffs).
- Automate urgent rollback across heterogeneous planes (hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private VPCs) with tenant-priority ordering and K/V cache reconciliation.
- Provide customer-facing comms and prescriptive remediation steps for SRE/Support to use.
- Postmortem checklist including regression test sets, replayable repro steps, and follow-ups.

Proposed approach:
1) Canary triage checklist: collect model version, variant id, recent bundle diffs, sample traces, latency/quality deltas, and top-10 failing prompts (from quality monitors).
2) Containment: use traffic-slicing tooling to quarantine affected tenant slices; if unavailable, use a fast feature-gate to pin to previous variant.
3) Decision matrix: if quality delta > 15% on critical evals OR customer complaint escalates to P0, initiate coordinated rollback. For low-impact flakiness, attempt surgical hotpatch (patch LLM tokenization, prompt preprocessor fixes) on canary only.
4) Rollback choreography: orchestrate three-phase rollback: (a) freeze new routing decisions, (b) push rollback request to controller plane with ordered targets (hosted -> dedicated -> private), (c) reconcile KV cache mismatches and warm caches to avoid cold-start regressions.
5) Customer comms: templated email/slack messages with ETA, mitigations, and postmortem promise. Include step-by-step guidance for Dedicated/Private customers who operate their own control plane.

Out-of-scope: deep model training fixes or long-running retraining jobs. Long-term automation of every heterogeneous private endpoint upgrade (this ticket focuses on emergency flows and runbooks).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented flipbook exists in Confluence with the triage checklist, decision matrix, rollback choreography, and customer templates.
2) Automated rollback script tested end-to-end in staging across hosted and a simulated dedicated pool (runbooks contain command snippets).
3) Support & SRE have approved comms templates and run a tabletop drill that completes containment and customer notification within the target SLA (30 minutes).
4) Playbook contains explicit KV cache reconciliation steps and at least one automation hook to warm caches after rollback.
5) Post-incident checklist added to incident tracker and linked to the runbook.
test_plan: Staging validation plan: (1) Deploy model variant A->B in staging with synthetic failing prompts injected; (2) Trigger flipbook containment and run automated rollback script; (3) Verify KV cache reconciliation and warmup; (4) Run end-to-end quality eval suite and confirm metrics return to baseline. Record runbook timestamps and telemetry to verify <30m SLA in drill.
communication_templates: Slack short notice: 'We are investigating an elevated integrity regression in canary for model {model} affecting {tenant_slice}. Containment actions underway. ETA for mitigation: {eta}.'

Customer email template: 'We detected a regression after a model rollout which may affect your traffic. We are rolling back the change for your tenant. Estimated time to resolution: {eta}. We will follow up with a post-incident report.'
